nodes.label: Extraction Subagent Prompt
nodes.rationale: The verbatim prompt handed to each semantic subagent, with FILE_LIST, CHUNK_NUM, TOTAL_CHUNKS, DEEP_MODE, and CHUNK_PATH substituted. Loaded only when a chunk holds a doc, paper, or image; a pure-code corpus never reads it. CHUNK_PATH must be absolute because Write resolves relative paths against an undefined cwd and the file would be silently lost.

nodes.label: Node ID Format Rule
nodes.rationale: {full-repo-relative-path-stem}_{entity}, every directory level kept, lowercase [a-z0-9_] only. Using just the filename or only the immediate parent creates orphan ghost-duplicate nodes because the ID must match what the AST extractor generates. Chunk or sequence suffixes are forbidden: IDs must be deterministic from the label alone so the same entity resolves identically regardless of which chunk processed it.

nodes.label: Confidence Score Rubric
nodes.rationale: EXTRACTED is always 1.0; INFERRED must pick exactly one of 0.95/0.85/0.75/0.65/0.55; AMBIGUOUS is 0.1-0.3. Discrete values replaced a continuous range because production showed a bimodal collapse (>50% at 0.5, >40% at 0.85+) — models follow discrete rubrics better. If nothing fits, mark the edge AMBIGUOUS rather than scoring below 0.4.

nodes.label: Hyperedge Rule
nodes.rationale: Used only when three or more nodes participate in a shared concept, flow, or pattern that pairwise edges do not already capture — implementers of a protocol, all steps of an auth flow, one coherent paper section. Maximum three per chunk.

nodes.label: source_file Verbatim Rule
nodes.rationale: Every node, edge, and hyperedge must copy the FILE_LIST path character-for-character — no basename shortening, re-relativizing, or separator changes — because the engine canonicalizes downstream. This keeps the full build and incremental --update on the same base so build_merge's replace-on-re-extract matches the existing node instead of accumulating a duplicate.

edges.source_location: This must match the ID the AST extractor generates
so build_merge's replace-on-re-extract matches the existing node
